subject: Trading
title: The Flash Crash of 2010
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Flash Crash of 2010.

hook.text: On May 6, 2010, the Dow Jones fell nearly 1,000 points in minutes—then recovered almost entirely. No one understood why.

buildup.text: At 2:32 PM, a massive sell order hit the market. Algorithms began selling into each other in a feedback loop.

discovery.text: Some stocks traded at $0.01 while others hit $100,000. Market prices became meaningless for several minutes.

twist.text: A single trader, Navinder Sarao, was later accused of contributing with spoofing—placing fake orders to move prices.

climax.text: The flash crash revealed how fragile modern electronic markets are when algorithms interact unpredictably.

punchline.text: Machines can crash markets faster than humans can react.

quiz.question: What caused the 2010 flash crash?
options: Algorithms selling into each other in a feedback loop
